LETTER TO THE EDITORS
Deab Bhothers:

Yesterday, the Xi Chapter received a letter from the Foster Parents' Plan for War Children,
Inc.,** asking us to write them a letter explaining the benefits derived from "adopting" a Foster
Child, which they could distribute to you and the rest of the Fraternity. This is in. response.
The workings of this Plan are simple: The _
,

Chapter sends a small sum of money to a ^tv '*''
poverty-stricken child overseas and one
Brother, in behalf of the Chapter, enters into
correspondence with him, exchanging letters
monthly.
The Xi Chapter "adopted" Norbert Wagner
in September, 1953, Born May, 1941, the

younger of two sons in a refugee family liv
ing a few miles from Lake Constance, which
is on the Swiss-German border. Norbert's
father disappeared on the Eastern front in
1945; no trace of him has since been found.
Norbert, mother and brother were de
his
ported from their native Czechoslovakia in
1945, in accordance with the PotsdamTruman Treaty, and Hved in great misery in
the Russian Zone of Germany until they es
caped to the American Zone in 1949. Botli
boys have had tuberculosis. Tlieir mother
works in the fields when her health permits
and it is a heart warming thought that it is
the Xi's money contribution which enables
her to keep the family together.
In the years since the "adoption," we have
watched Norbert's growth and been delighted
by his warm letters of news and thanks. Our
payments of $15.00 a month were divided
between food packages from the U.S.A. and
a
clothing allowance which buys all Norbert's
clothes.
We would not bother to send this letter
Norbert Wagner, Foster Son of the XI Chapter.
if we did not feel that this Plan has been a
very worthwhile experience. Overseas gifts
without personal contact are often poorly received and sometimes resented, but here both
giver and receiver can see the progress that is being made and can truly appreciate each
other's position. Such exchange "blesseth him that gives and him that takes" and is in full
accord with our motto and principles.
We have high faith in the integrity of the organization. It has shown itself conscientious,
experienced and careful. Through it, the Xi Chapter has enjoyed its contact with the Foster
Child and feels that the other Chapters which have not yet "adopted" a child would do
deeply
well to give it a try.
